headline: Dry weather holds as both regions warm sharply by Wednesday
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: High pressure keeps Danville and the Bluegrass sunny and rain-free through Tuesday. As the high shifts east, southerly flow drives a pronounced warm-up Wednesday. Clear, calm conditions may allow brief shallow fog in favored valleys early Tuesday.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No hazardous weather expected; patchy valley fog possible late tonight
days.forecast: Sunny and dry after the cool start. Light north wind generally stays below 8 mph. Skies remain mostly clear tonight, with temperatures falling into the upper 40s and patchy shallow fog possible in favored valleys toward daybreak.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: Brief patchy fog possible before 8 AM, mainly in valleys
days.forecast: Any shallow valley fog should dissipate shortly after sunrise, followed by sunny skies. Wind remains very light from the east before turning southeast Tuesday night. The night will be clear and noticeably milder than Monday night.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Sunny and much warmer as southerly flow strengthens around the departing high. South wind remains modest, generally 3–8 mph. Wednesday night stays partly cloudy, dry and much milder, with lows mainly in the middle 60s.

kentucky.bottomLine: Confidence is high in a dry 72-hour period. The key change is the temperature climb from the upper 70s Monday to the upper 80s Wednesday. The only meaningful short-term uncertainty is localized valley fog early Tuesday and the exact Wednesday high.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather; moderate-high on Wednesday temperatures and localized fog

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Clemson and Central remain sunny, dry and quiet under high pressure through Wednesday. Afternoon temperatures rise a few degrees each day, reaching the middle 80s Wednesday, while light wind and clear nights keep mornings comfortable.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Monday
days.forecast: Sunny and dry with a very light west to northwest wind. Skies remain mostly clear tonight as wind turns light northeast, allowing temperatures to settle into the upper 50s around Clemson and Central.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny and a little warmer. East wind remains around 2–5 mph, with no meaningful moisture return or convective signal. Tuesday night stays clear and calm with lows near 60.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and warmer, with afternoon temperatures reaching the middle 80s. Wind remains light from the east. Mostly clear conditions persist Wednesday night, with a gradual rise in overnight humidity but no rain through the 72-hour window.

upstate.bottomLine: Confidence is high in three dry, mostly sunny days with no organized hazardous-weather signal. Temperatures rise gradually from around 80 Monday to the middle 80s Wednesday.

sourceNotes: NWS point forecasts were generated at 7:05 AM EDT for Danville and 7:47 AM EDT for Clemson. Official airport observations span 7:15–7:25 AM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 6:45 AM and 6:43 AM EDT, respectively. Both support dry weather through the 72-hour period. Louisville highlights the Wednesday warm-up as southerly flow develops; Greenville-Spartanburg reports good guidance agreement on dry weather and a steady midweek warming trend.
The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the 7:47 AM EDT check. This official-alert status is separate from the independent analysis.

NOMADS inventories checked before issuance showed the 10Z HRRR complete through forecast hour 18, the 11Z RAP ingesting with the 10Z cycle complete, 06Z NAM through hour 84, NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS through hour 384, and the 06Z GEFS mean beyond hour 72. The latest complete ECMWF deterministic cycle available for verification was 00Z.

College of DuPage NEXLAB panels were checked directly. The 11:46 AM UTC visible satellite showed both forecast regions largely clear, and the 11:50 AM UTC Southeast radar mosaic showed no organized echoes over either region. NAM Nest simulated reflectivity remained quiet locally through Wednesday afternoon.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.
Radar and satellite links remain external and live; the existing Google Sites radar section is not modified by this candidate.
